A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDAD research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MVTec and VisA experiments, cross-dataset evaluations, component ablations and iSVD memory/runtime analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same gradient projection, iterative SVD, anomaly-masked network, losses and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image-level anomaly detection and pixel-level localization on MVTec and VisA, including continual learning within datasets and in both cross-dataset directions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in each corresponding comparison table, including the UniAD variants, UCAD, IUF, DiAD and ControlNet where originally evaluated. Citation changes do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The incremental schedules, 256-by-256 inputs, 500/100-epoch training budgets, 10-step DDIM inference and AUROC/AUPR/PRO/FM evaluation remain unchanged, including appendix settings.

E4.justification: The CDM/AMN ablation, iSVD projection validation, threshold sensitivity, block-size memory/runtime analysis and qualitative case studies are retained without substantive revisions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical entries, and the plotted trends and qualitative findings remain unchanged. For example, CDAD's MVTec setting 4 image/pixel A-AUROC remains 94.9/95.7.

T1.justification: The linear-transitivity lemma and proof, gradient-projection derivation and Appendix B memory-saving analysis remain mathematically unchanged. Appendix equation layout adjustments do not change the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about continual diffusion, iSVD memory efficiency, anomaly-masked conditioning and first-place performance in 17/18 settings.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same mechanism interpretations, stability/plasticity discussion, iSVD approximation-loss qualification and additional runtime cost. No substantive limitation or applicability boundary is added.

D1.justification: The code link, model and feature-extractor details, preprocessing, patch-perturbation parameters and 10% old-task sampling recipe are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

R1.justification: Six cited works are added, including PromptAD, VS-Boost and CTNet; five are removed, including PNI, DDPM and AnomalyXFusion. Section 2 briefly connects generation to other visual tasks, while the central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 corrects the iSVD reference from Figure 3.3 to Figure 2 and changes 'quantitative' to 'qualitative' in Section 4.3. Author information is updated and acknowledgments are added; the narrative structure is otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Table sizing and spacing, figure placement and appendix equation layout receive limited adjustments. The same displays are retained, and tighter layout brings the complete conclusion onto page 8.

improvement.justification: The corrected cross-reference and qualitative wording provide small editorial benefits. However, the scientific argument, theoretical and experimental support, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including the appendices. The citation and layout revisions leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
